audioScript: I've been going back and forth about whether to buy a new laptop or fix my old one.

choices.text: I go back and forth to campus by bike.
How old is it? Repairs aren't always worth it.
My new laptop arrived yesterday.
Fixing breakfast only takes me about ten minutes.

explanation: The key responds to the speaker's indecision with a relevant question; choice A uses 'back and forth' as literal travel, and choice D reuses 'fix'.

audioScript: It looks like the reserve shelf is missing half the readings for my seminar.

choices.text: I missed the seminar last week.
Half the class reserved seats early.
Your professor may have posted them online.
It looks like rain this afternoon.

explanation: The key offers a likely explanation for the missing readings; choices A, B, and D echo 'missing', 'reserve', and 'it looks like'.

audioScript: Have you had any luck getting the campus Wi-Fi to work on your phone?

choices.text: Good luck on your exam today!
Only after I forgot the network and reconnected.
My phone is almost two years old.
Yes, I work on campus now.

explanation: The key reports success and how it was done; choice A echoes 'luck', and choice D uses 'work' to mean a job.

audioScript: I heard the computer lab is going to start charging for color printing.

choices.text: I heard a strange noise in the lab last night.
My phone is charging in the lab.
Then I'll stick to black and white for drafts.
The lab is painted a nice color this year.

explanation: The key draws a sensible plan from the news; choice B uses 'charging' for a battery.

audioScript: I'd be happy to lend you my old textbook, though it's a couple of editions behind.

choices.text: Thanks. I'll check that the chapters match first.
I'm happy with my new apartment.
Editions are printed every few years.
A couple of friends are behind on rent.

explanation: The key accepts the offer while addressing the concern about the edition; choice C comments on editions without replying to the offer.

audioScript: I had no idea the library lends out cameras and microphones.

choices.text: I lent him my camera on Monday.
No idea is too small to share.
Neither did I until my media project.
Microphones pick up a lot of noise.

explanation: The key shares the speaker's surprise; choice A shifts to a personal loan, and choice B echoes 'no idea'.

audioScript: What's the point of buying the access code if the homework is optional?

choices.text: The quizzes are graded, and they need it too.
The point is marked on the left side.
Buy it at the front counter.
The homework was due on Monday.

explanation: The key gives the real reason the code is needed; choice B takes 'point' literally, and choice C answers 'where'.

audioScript: Maybe you should back up your thesis before the system update tonight.

choices.text: My back has been sore all week from the gym.
The last update finished early on Tuesday morning.
Good thinking. I'd hate to lose a year's work.
Thesis defenses usually happen in May and June.

explanation: The key accepts the advice with a reason; choice A misreads 'back' as a body part, and choice B contradicts the time frame.

audioScript: It's strange that the bookstore closes right when classes let out.

choices.text: Let me out at the next stop.
Strangers ask me for directions a lot.
The bookstore closed my account.
It is. Maybe they're short on staff.

explanation: The key agrees and offers a possible reason; choices A and B echo 'let out' and 'strange' with unrelated meanings.

audioScript: The IT help desk keeps giving me the runaround about my email account.

choices.text: I ran around the track twice.
My email address is really long and hard to spell.
Have you tried emailing the IT manager directly?
They gave me a nice gift for my birthday.

explanation: The speaker means they are being sent from person to person, and the key suggests going higher; choice A takes 'runaround' literally.

audioScript: Did the librarian say whether we can renew the laptop over the phone?

choices.text: The phone is on the librarian's desk.
Yes, I renewed my lease.
We can say goodbye later.
She said we have to bring it in.

explanation: The key reports the librarian's answer; choice B says yes but talks about a lease, and choice A echoes 'phone' and 'librarian'.

audioScript: That online tutorial made the citation manager seem a lot easier than it is.

choices.text: The tutorial was posted last night.
My manager is easy to work with.
Tell me about it. I gave up halfway.
Online classes seem easier to me.

explanation: 'Tell me about it' agrees that the tool is harder than it looked; choice B takes 'manager' as a boss.

audioScript: You wouldn't happen to have a spare charger for this kind of laptop, would you?

choices.text: Sorry, mine only fits the older models.
This kind of weather is unusual.
I charged my phone last night.
Yes, I happened to see her.

explanation: The key politely declines and explains why; choice D says yes but echoes 'happen' with no charger in sight.

audioScript: The interlibrary loan request I put in last month finally came through.

choices.text: Loan payments start after graduation.
I'll put it on the request list.
Great. Now you can finish your literature review.
The library came through a hard year.

explanation: The key reacts to the good news with its consequence; choice A takes 'loan' as money, and choice D uses 'came through' differently.
